title: When you land
body:
Fukuoka Airport's domestic and international terminals are separate buildings, linked by a free shuttle bus (every 5–6 min at peak, 6–15 min off-peak). The Kuko (Airport) subway line only stops at the Domestic Terminal, so international arrivals take the shuttle first.

From the Domestic Terminal, the subway reaches Hakata Station in ≈5 min (≈¥260) and Tenjin in ≈11 min (≈¥260) — one of the shortest airport-to-downtown rides in Japan. Register everyone's passport in Visit Japan Web before departure to speed up immigration and customs; paper arrival/customs cards are still accepted if anyone skips it.

title: Local essentials
body:
Japan runs on 100V power with US-style Type A/B plugs — no adapter needed for US devices, though a few high-wattage appliances may need a voltage converter. Tipping isn't practiced anywhere, including restaurants and yatai — a service charge is never expected and offering cash tips can cause confusion.

Japan is exceptionally low-crime; the practical safety concerns for this trip are jaywalking habits (Japan enforces crosswalks) and October's occasional lingering typhoon activity — check forecasts a few days out. Convenience stores (7-Eleven, Lawson, FamilyMart) are everywhere in Hakata/Tenjin for basics, ATMs, and quick food.

title: Entry & documents
body:
US passport holders enter Japan visa-free for tourism, stays up to 90 days — no visa application needed for this trip. This assumes all 8 travelers hold US passports, which the intake didn't explicitly confirm; if anyone in the group carries a different passport, their entry rule needs its own check before booking.

Bring proof of onward/return travel and be ready to state your accommodation address on arrival. Declare cash over ¥1,000,000 at customs. A few high-wattage appliances aside, no other paperwork is required beyond the passport itself.

title: Phone & data
body: Fukuoka Airport's International Terminal (1F, landside) has a Sakura Mobile counter (7:00–21:00) selling SIM cards and renting pocket wifi routers, plus a second Global WiFi/Ninja WiFi counter. For a group of 8, an eSIM bought and activated before departure (Sakura Mobile, Ubigi, Airalo all serve Japan) skips the counter queue entirely — worth doing individually before you fly rather than lining up 8-deep at the airport.

title: Booking checklist
body: Nothing on this itinerary needs an advance-purchase timed ticket — Dazaifu Tenmangu is free, Kyushu National Museum and Nokonoshima Island Park sell same-day, and yatai don't take reservations. The checklist below is what actually needs sorting before you land.
checklist: Accommodation — confirm it sleeps/splits a party of 8 sensibly
Airport transfer — subway is simplest; confirm terminal (domestic vs. international)
Register everyone in Visit Japan Web
Each traveler's eSIM or data plan activated before departure
Confirm every traveler's passport country (see the traveler question)
